title: Adaptive kernel selector and staged capture warmup for noisy multi-stream inference
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem: In high-concurrency multi-tenant workloads we observe intermittent cuda graph capture failures and nondeterministic replay correctness when streams with heterogeneous sequence lengths interleave captures. Root causes identified in prior triage: (1) aggressive kernel binding picks specialized kernels that are optimal for long sequences but brittle under short/prefill windows, (2) capture warmup occurs mid-flight causing partial graph segments, and (3) no lightweight probe/fallback exists to detect and recover incompatible kernel paths at replay.

Goal: Implement an adaptive kernel selector that uses lightweight runtime telemetry to pick robust kernels for prefill and early decode phases, combined with a staged capture warmup flow that aligns capture boundaries to epoch windows and introduces a probe-and-fallback path before committing graphs to persistent replay. The change should reduce capture-related failures by >= 90% on our noise workloads, add <5% median latency overhead for steady-state inference, and provide clear operational signals for fallback activations.

Scope: runtime changes (kernel selector + probe API), capture orchestration (staged warmup & epoch alignment), telemetry (probe/fallback counters, kernel compatibility events), unit/e2e tests (simulated interleaved streams), and a gradual rollout plan with observability dashboards and automatic rollback on quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive kernel selector chooses robust kernel variant for prefill 99% of the time on short-sequence workloads
Capture failure rate on noisy multi-stream test harness reduced by >= 90% compared to baseline
Probe-and-fallback path triggers a graph-free slow path with successful decode in <200ms when incompatibility detected
Telemetry emits kernel_compatibility_event, probe_activation, fallback_activation metrics; dashboards created
Integration tests cover: mixed-length concurrent prefills, probe-triggered recovery, and replay determinism across 1000 randomized seeds
No increase >5% in 99th percentile latency for production-like steady workload after rollout
implementation_notes: Add KernelTelemetry struct (runtime counter + last_successful_variant) with lock-free updates
Introduce KernelProbe API: run short verification decode on new kernel variants during warmup with timeout 50ms
Staged warmup flow: (1) short probe decode, (2) ephemeral capture window, (3) persistent capture commit after N successful probes or T ms
Fallback policy: on probe failure increment fallback counter and route subsequent requests to conservative kernel path and unrolled decode until stable
Compatibility matrix persisted per model-version+hw SKU to avoid repeated probes at scale
Expose metrics: kernel_probe_latency_ms, kernel_probe_success, kernel_fallback_count, capture_commit_latency_ms
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Probe adds latency to cold-request path. Mitigation: keep probe small (<=50ms) and selectively enable only for short-sequence/prefill requests
Risk: Increased complexity in capture orchestration could regress existing graph commits. Mitigation: comprehensive e2e harness and staged rollout with kill-switch flag
Risk: Compatibility matrix staleness across driver/firmware updates. Mitigation: bump matrix TTL and attach automated re-probe jobs on node image updates
tests: Unit: kernel selector heuristics on synthetic sequence-length distributions
Integration: multi-stream harness with 256 concurrent streams, randomized seq lengths, simulate preemption and GPU context switches
Fuzz: 1000 randomized capture/replay cycles verifying KV cache integrity and token-level deterministic outputs
Perf: A/B baseline vs adaptive selector on 1M request sample measuring P50/P95/P99 latency and token throughput
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated into runtime binary (default off)
Canary: Enable for 1% of hosted traffic in region us-west-2 for 24 hours with auto-watchers
Ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% daily with health checks at each step
Abort criteria: capture failure rate > baseline or P99 latency regression >5% over 1 hour
Postmortem: collect probe/fallback traces, attach to nightly regression job if abort triggered
notes: Initial triage found reproducer harness in infra-qe with two synthetic models (gpt-small-ish, decoder-16k) — using that for early validation
Proposed conservative kernel variants are existing optimized kernels compiled with different block sizes; no new kernels required for MVP
Mateo to open draft PR linking to the probe API and telemetry schemata by 2026-03-10
Coordinate with infra scheduling team to ensure probe jobs are not preempted in Dedicated pools
